product_target.statement: Moria is a reusable Rust voxel-world substrate delivered through public crate interfaces and exercised by a minimal non-game validation executable; current deliverables are substrate capabilities only, not any particular game.

documents.rationale: Repository orientation that points at the mixed program brief as the product definition and states that only current substrate commitments are deliverables.
Defines the current Moria substrate product, public boundary, correctness and validation commitments, non-goals, and embeds later-consumer vision as non-authorizing context.
Supports the program brief by describing the reusable consumer surface without adding deliverables or expanding product scope.

claims.statement: Moria is the reusable voxel-world substrate defined by the mixed project brief; only the current substrate commitments are deliverables in this repository.

Moria is a reusable Rust voxel-world substrate consumed through public crate interfaces by games and by a minimal validation executable; this repository delivers the substrate, not any particular game.
The current product owns deterministic seed-based generation; generation is deterministic for the same versioned parameters and seed.

External consumers can create and identify a world, request bounded regions, observe readiness, query material truth, submit bounded edits, and persist deltas; consumers must not reach into storage, meshing, or scheduler internals.

The validation executable uses exactly the public interfaces, may provide a free-fly camera and diagnostics, is not a game prototype, and owns no privileged world path; headless fixtures cover generation, query, mutation, persistence, and lifecycle, and a small visual fixture proves an external consumer can render and edit through the public API.

locator.heading: Current public boundary; Current validation commitments

claims.statement: Mutation is admitted through a bounded command API and committed atomically; persistence restores the same authoritative material state; derived meshes and diagnostics never become authoritative world state; streaming bounds resident work and exposes observable lifecycle states.

Moria does not implement game rules, combat, inventory, AI, narrative systems, characters, animation, authored levels, or production content; references to possible consumers explain interface pressure only.

After the reusable substrate ships, a separate Product One repository may place a third-person explorer in a generated region; that later material does not authorize a player controller, character mesh, animation clips, curated route, or game asset in Moria.
The later Product One vision may include a dense mixed forest among hills, river, and cave scenery; forest population workload and related game assets are not authorized as Moria deliverables.

The interface reference supports the Moria program brief without adding deliverables and describes world identity, readiness and bounded material queries, bounded mutation commands, streaming lifecycle states, delta persistence, registered objects, and diagnostics.
